ticket.title: Verify gates: unchecked plan steps, unresolved children, manual receipts, state deletion
ticket.description:
Four refusals, each from a measured failure. (1) Refuse to verify a task whose plan has unchecked steps: SP-6 closed with 0 of 6 and a manual receipt. (2) Refuse to close an epic while a child is unresolved, reading the rollup because children may live in another repository. (3) Refuse --manual when the task has an executable verification chain, since verify now runs the chain and a manual receipt attests nothing. (4) Refuse a commit that deletes tracked files under .gaugeblock/ unless it cites a decision record: ten repositories retired their repo-local ledgers on 2026-11-06 as routine hygiene, and an ADR requirement would have forced the sentence that exposes the circularity, namely that the ledgers froze because nothing wrote to them and were deleted because they were frozen.

PARTIAL 2026-11-08 (commit 347ae5d): refusal 1 of 4 is live.

verify now refuses when the task's own plan has unchecked steps, naming each open step. A task with no plan,
and a plan whose steps are all complete, pass - the plan is an optional stronger promise, and requiring one
would punish the honest small ticket.

This is the refusal that would have stopped the failure that motivated the ticket: SP-6 verified with 0 of 6
steps and a record claiming delivery of a fleet of distributed ledgers that did not exist.

The other three, each with the reason it is not in this commit:
  - epic closure with unresolved children needs the workspace rollup to see children in other repositories
    (SP-36);
  - --manual alongside an executable chain: the chain is resolved inside receipts::build, so the check belongs
    there rather than at the entry point;
  - a commit deleting tracked .gaugeblock state without a decision record is a miter audit rule, in another
    repository.
acceptance_criteria: a perf task cannot be verified without a before/after measurement recorded in the commit, the task and a durable document (law 12), so the kind added in GB-343 does not license an unmeasured claim

REFUSAL 2 OF 4 LIVE 2026-11-08 (commit 1858c32).

verify now refuses `verifier: manual` when a chain resolves for the task, and names the chain. Three tests: refused
with the chain named; an explicit --verifier accepted; and a manual receipt fine when nothing is configured.

The escape hatch is deliberate, not a loophole: a ticket verified on a machine without the toolchain must be able to
say who attested it. The rule targets the default, which is the path taken without thinking - and SP-6 is what
taking it looks like.

Still owed: epic closure with unresolved children (needs the rollup, which SP-36 half-built) and the ADR-citation
gate for deleting tracked state (a miter rule, in another repository).

REFUSAL 3 OF 4 LIVE 2026-11-08 (commit ca0e733).

An epic can no longer be certified while a child of it is open. Children are found through the edges they carry,
not a list the epic holds, and the refusal names each open child with its status.

Finished means verified or archived: archived is a state rather than a status, and a task retired without
verification was dealt with whatever the outcome. A feature with children is unaffected - the rule is about what an
epic claims.

Scope is stated rather than implied: only children in the same store are visible, because since ADR 0009 the rest
live in other repositories. The refusal is honest about what it can prove instead of silent about what it cannot,
and extending it across stores is the workspace rollup's remaining half (SP-36).

One of four remains: the ADR-citation gate for deleting tracked .gaugeblock state, which is a miter rule in another
repository.
